Nobody considered the consequences of retrofitting an antique car with a temporal engine. After all, space and time are related so by moving yourself through time you're moving yourself through space as well. So an antique car was retrofitted with a temporal engine.

During the first test drive, nothing unusual happened. The car started just fine, and it moved. It worked like a dream. The same happened during the rest of the test drives, and after each one some small calibrations were made to ensure that the performance would be flawless. It wasn't until it was sold to a pensioner that the car disappeared off the lot forever. Maybe it was too tight of a bolt, or maybe that final calibration put it off spec. Regardless, it was gone, and the pensioner with it.

It endured three hundred years of aging, along with the pensioner inside. The temporal engine had too much horsepower, and instead of pushing the car and passenger through space-time it instead pushed the duo through time itself, but without any protection. Fortunately the engine blew out at the three hundred year mark, but by then the antique car looked antique again, and the pensioner was merely dust in the interior and some bones scattered on the floor.

the engine compartment had the most room with the best hiding spot. the two legged ones had already stripped off the four round parts and the engine. i knew about the engine, since the days when mahakatraveh had translated part of the bound papers in the odd metal box. but, he stayed out too long one day, the two legged ones found him, or that was what the sounds implied.

it was a hot day with the heat in the compartment. the compartment had already been sealed from the harsh sun with nesting spit, and dirt sealed off the bottom of the metal thing as it had sunk down in age. at night the dried nesting spit glowed a faint green, you had to be careful about leaking light out. i lazily readjusted my tail in the space, scales rasping the metal. accommodation was a rarity and a find after the initial arrival and chaos.

my kin was a, reactive, bunch. a shame we and the two legged ones both paid for it. the sun of the planet was even worse, and i count it a blessing me and my kin arrived at night, but for now nighttime was still hours away. my ears bristled up as other sounds became clear. footsteps, rummaging, the sound of metal. as the end of a prying tool snapped through the nesting spittle sealing the compartments lid, spines unfurled, claws jutted. the lid began lifting.

It is also used in the Orwellian sense of doublethink where "social" actually means "authoritarian" and support for the orthodox authority's changing position regarding justice.

Doublethink is the act of ordinary people simultaneously accepting two mutually contradictory beliefs as correct, often in distinct social contexts. Doublethink is related to, but differs from, hypocrisy and neutrality. Somewhat related but almost the opposite is cognitive dissonance, where contradictory beliefs cause conflict in one's mind. Doublethink is notable due to a lack of cognitive dissonance — thus the person is completely unaware of any conflict or contradiction.

George Orwell created the word doublethink in his dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949); doublethink is part of newspeak. In the novel, its origin within the typical citizen is unclear; while it could be partly a product of Big Brother's formal brainwashing programmes, the novel explicitly shows people learning Doublethink and newspeak due to peer pressure and a desire to "fit in", or gain status within the Party — to be seen as a loyal Party Member. In the novel, for someone to even recognize – let alone mention – any contradiction within the context of the Party line was akin to blasphemy, and could subject that someone to possible disciplinary action and to the instant social disapproval of fellow Party Members.
